source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, General Information and Lubrication, p.0-10

procedures.title: Engine crankcase oil: capacity and viscosity
notes: SAE 5W and 5W-20 are not for sustained high-speed driving.
SAE 30 and 20W-40 may be used above 90°F.
SAE 10W-40 may be used between 0 and 90°F.
Use only oils certified by the supplier as meeting the automakers' sequence tests or GM Standard 6041-M; the container will say so.

procedures.title: Engine oil level: check
steps: After running the engine, wait a few minutes for oil to drain back before checking.
Keep the level between the "Add Oil" and "Full" lines on the gauge rod.
Check often and top up as needed.

procedures.title: Engine oil and filter: change intervals
steps: Drain and refill the crankcase every 4 months or 6000 miles, whichever comes first, under normal driving.
Drain only when the engine is fully warm, so contaminants come out with the oil.
Replace the filter at the first oil change and at every second change after that.

specs.what: oil change, heavy duty (start-stop or long idling)

notes: Change more often under prolonged dusty conditions.

Crankcase dilution: fuel and water vapor condense in a cold engine and form acids that etch piston pins, cam bearings and other parts. The thermostat, coolant bypass, exhaust manifold heat control, automatic choke and crankcase ventilation all reduce it.

procedures.title: Manifold heat control valve: check
steps: Every 6,000 miles, check that the valve moves freely.
If the shaft sticks, free it with GM Manifold Heat Control Solvent or equivalent.
